feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector specialization. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with some structural overlap between skills sections and limited quantified outcomes beyond platform scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative and career progression within NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility through concrete platform details: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools like GA4, BigQuery, and Drupal.  
- Writing is polished and professional, with strong domain positioning in digital modernization, editorial systems, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scale and responsibilities, e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption rates, campaign results, or cost/time savings.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “social, and multimedia” vs. “web, email, social and video”); “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—consider “French (A2, improving).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make more specific: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years driving web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Add scale or scope from recent roles, e.g., “Led a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views and 50+ publishers.”
- Replace “builds the platforms” phrasing with stronger outcome-oriented language like “modernizes,” “scales,” or “leads transformation of.”
- Consider trimming “multimedia production” or “AI-enabled user experiences” unless these are essential target-role keywords; they are already supported elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader,” “platforms,” “governance,” and “content operations” repeat the subtitle and core competencies.
- The long list of capabilities mirrors later skills sections; the intro should emphasize positioning and scale, not inventory.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work history. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Prioritize the most senior/recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation/integration.
- Replace broader items with more specific, higher-impact phrasing, e.g.: “Editorial governance and publishing systems,” “Analytics, dashboarding, and reporting infrastructure,” “Multimedia production, studio, and livestream operations.”
- Suggested version: Enterprise web modernization • Editorial governance and publishing systems • Analytics, dashboarding, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Multi-channel digital communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production, studio, and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” and “Workflow automation and platform integration” repeat Topline Skills/Technical + IT almost verbatim.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with the header and Topline Skills; consider keeping just one of those formulations.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinct and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Emphasize outcomes or scale where possible: e.g., “improving policy-content discovery,” “built for ongoing campaign expansion,” or audience/use context.
- Use consistent action verbs and structure; for example, start each with “Built,” “Developed,” or “Led.”
- Replace “10×20-foot” with “10 x 20-foot” for style consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series overlap with current/previous NACo bullets; this footer should highlight distinct project flavor, not restate role responsibilities.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most differentiated item; consider leading with it to reduce repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web modernization, and communications operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-focused points, e.g.:
- “Designed and improved cross-channel digital workflows, analytics, and governance systems to support coordinated communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Built Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search planning, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”
- Replace generic phrases like “deliver technical troubleshooting” with stronger verbs and clearer ownership: built, implemented, optimized, advised, led.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, or engagement/search improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording overlaps heavily with the NACo Director role on governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement.
- Microsite and AI search bullets may duplicate the “Recent Projects” section; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-oriented.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership impact in one line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget management.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing, especially for email/social, studio build, and governance: audience growth, production volume, cost savings, faster publishing, improved reporting cadence, or stakeholder adoption.
- Tighten phrasing by removing generic verbs like “strengthened” and “expanded” unless paired with a result; combine tools into one concise analytics bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization and systems.
- Video/studio language may duplicate older production roles; emphasize building organizational capability, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving coordination for editorial and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten bullets and use action/result structure: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications operations across web, email, social and video” is repeated in the Director of Digital Media role; keep this version more execution-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership areas not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & publishing operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use parallel noun phrases; avoid mixed constructions like “audience-focused content planning” beside broader leadership terms.
- Consider swapping “multi-channel communications leadership” for “cross-channel communications operations” if you want stronger alignment with recent role language.
- If space allows, prioritize differentiators such as governance, modernization, and public-sector context over generic “content planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms most tied to recent impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to a sharper, priority-ordered summary: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences • WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages”
- Put Drupal first and group older/secondary platforms later, since recent roles and projects are clearly Drupal-led.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based content systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, use “CMS platforms, integrations & automation” as the heading to better match the content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates many exact tools already listed in “Technical + IT”; keep this section higher-level and save full tool inventory for that section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep wording distinct or remove from one section.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Use grouped phrasing: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic items with stronger business-facing terms: “KPI framework development,” “executive dashboarding,” “performance and SEO analysis,” “insight-driven optimization”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity - KPI framework development and executive dashboarding - SEO, performance analysis and conversion optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive dashboarding” or “executive reporting.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value production leadership and event delivery rather than basic task labels.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools/tasks to scope and level: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event execution”
- If you want more impact, add scale where true: “Livestream and hybrid event production for national advocacy programming and member events”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a broader phrase that signals ownership, not just execution: “End-to-end video production”
- Keep only 4–5 bullets and use parallel noun phrases for cleaner scanning

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording exactly
- Specific tools like PTZ systems may be better kept in Technical + IT unless they are a clear differentiator for target roles

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this item to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeating the same names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by proficiency/usage: **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint / Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add context to the lead platform: **Drupal 7/10** or **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views environment)** to tie directly to recent impact.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- Keep only platforms here; leave implementation details to the coding/tools sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Topline Skills entry “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- GitHub Pages may feel minor versus enterprise platforms; keep it only if it supports a portfolio or lightweight site-building narrative.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use and modernize older terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery • Technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Deployment & automation: GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they date the section without adding value.
- Group skills by function rather than listing flat keywords; this improves scanability and signals applied capability.
- If accurate, replace broad terms with stronger specifics, e.g., “REST API integrations,” “serverless scripting,” or “CI/CD automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- GitHub Actions and Cloudflare Workers are useful differentiators here, so keep them if space is limited.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and reads as a generic software list. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills, so it should emphasize systems actually used to drive operational impact.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to improve signal: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” so the category better matches the contents.
- Prioritize tools tied to recent work and remove weaker/general items if space is tight; keep Airtable, Power Automate, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams first.
- If accurate, add a light qualifier instead of a bare list: “Used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; they add less value than automation/project systems.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a generic tool list. Strengthen it by signaling enterprise-scale email/engagement capability and aligning terminology with the rest of the CV.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email, newsletter operations, audience engagement)**
- If space allows, add scope rather than more tools: **Used to support high-volume newsletter and member communications programs**
- Keep platform names only if they were meaningfully used in recent roles; otherwise drop the least relevant/oldest tool

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated “email/newsletters reaching tens of thousands” language in Work Experience; don’t restate outcomes here.
- “Engagement” is already implied in Core Competencies and multi-channel communications; avoid adding vague descriptors like “CRM” unless directly relevant.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the Director role bullets. Make it tighter and more capability-led, with only the most relevant tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation”
- Replace “A/B testing” with “Experimentation” only if you’ve directly run tests; otherwise remove it to avoid overstating.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for a stronger business outcome focus.
- Order by strategic weight and recency: analytics stack first, then insight/optimization capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one section or making this one tools-only and the other outcomes/capabilities.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating every platform elsewhere unless needed for ATS.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete outputs you can quantify.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience growth, email/social performance, or production volume.
- Tighten the close to show supervision without overstating management: “Produced livestreams and recurring video updates and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If space allows, split into 2 bullets: one for team/workflow foundation, one for website/content production impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” and workflow improvements overlap with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as the launch/origin of those efforts.
- Avoid broad “web, email, social, and multimedia” phrasing if the same channel list appears repeatedly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generically and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more concise and outcome-oriented: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading its planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or result: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast expanded member engagement.
- Consider splitting into 2 bullets for scanability rather than one paragraph.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research coordination + first podcast launch.
- Avoid broad claims about leading digital operations here, since stronger, more recent entries already cover that progression.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. In a senior CV, this section should emphasize tools only, not broader capabilities already proven elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Tighten to software/platforms and remove workflow-style phrases:  
  **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator**
- If you want to keep one capability marker, make it more technical and concise:  
  **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production systems**
- Consider renaming the heading to better match the content:
